### Explanation:

There are 6 Millennium Prize Questions. My Forecast is:

Autonomous Machine Intellience (AI) must be of a scale approaching Singularity - augmented by Chronimec Transparency. (By 2040, AI will advance Humanity, but that progress is halted by AI-risk.)

The short form forecast is simple. Given the original question formulation by the Clay Institute, I believe that within the time scales of this forecast, AI machines (ticks of 365 day time intervals) will contribute at least 1 identifying step in a correct formal proof for one of the Millennium Problems.

I use the word "step" to mean that AI systems will advance our understanding toward the whole proof. "Step" contrasts with the term "solution" in the sense that the final solution may require multiple informally identified steps.

The long form forecast is more complicated, involving specific historical events in human history that appear to warrant particular assumptions as also being events that will occur (or have already occurred) within the time frames of the forecasting question. If these particular assumptions happen, then a logical next consequence is inclusion of a solution to a Raymond Smullyan problem by a particular automata. The entire long form may or may not happen - my personal opinion is that most likely I am mistaken on one or more assumptions, and most likely the reinforcement learning machines utilized will not be involved in formulating an optimal solution to any of the Millennium Problems.

So defining reasonably occurring events: physiognomicity (1980s - 1990s) or futurism (2010s) or evangelism (2020s)

Now: Given these assumptions, why would a "tick" of AI (365 days) provide a step toward a resolution to a Millennium Prize Question? 

Rain and shine - skepticism of my Forecast that can be resolved by the Clay Institute discovery of a step toward a Millennium Problem proof, requiring a mathematical cadence in a non-deterministic information-form of Turing 1938 - March 2011. המון
As of 2025, I am quite sure that a mathematical proof asserted by AI for Fermat's Last Theorem has already been discovered and verified. (Please correct me if I am mistaken.) For brevity, this means that collaboration between AGI and humans was involved in that discovery.

On the subject of AGI not contributing to solving any of the aggressive-no-go Millennium Problems: 

* IMO, human cognitive workings is the closest we have to an AGI today. 
* I believe that if sufficient time is spent on the problem ($operatorname{P}nerset{=}operatorname{NP}$ problem), there is a possibility that one will occur on it within a human lifetime. 
* If this occurs before 2045, a portion of the claimant's proof is most likely also contributed by an AGI.

formatted_prompt:
<|im_start|>user
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

For each deadline, state your probability that this event will have occurred by then. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.<|im_end|>
